trust_boundaries: ingestion-to-processing: kafka_cluster to flink_cluster and spark_batch
storage-to-serving: data_lake_curated/data_warehouse to ml_model_registry and bi_dashboard
platform-to-all: iam_service and airflow_orchestrator to processing and storage tiers
architecture_summary.operational_context: Multi-cloud streaming and batch data pipeline — AWS Kinesis + GCP Pub/Sub sources, Kafka ingestion, Flink/Spark processing, multi-zone data lake, serving via ML endpoints and BI

threat_actors.name: Compromised External Data Source
threat_actors.motivation: Inject malicious or poisoned records into the ingestion pipeline to corrupt downstream analytics or ML model training
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Compromise of one of the four external source connectors (Kinesis, Pub/Sub, SFTP, or webhook)
non_capabilities: No direct access to Kafka admin API or broker configuration
No credentials for processing tier (Flink, Spark) or storage tier
No ability to read existing data lake contents directly
No access to IAM service or airflow orchestrator

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insider — Data Engineer
threat_actors.motivation: Exfiltrate confidential datasets from data warehouse or curated data lake for external sale
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate Airflow and Spark access used to stage and exfiltrate bulk data
non_capabilities: No access to ML model registry or serving endpoints
No ability to modify IAM policies directly
No root-level cloud storage access — scoped to specific buckets via IAM

threat_actors.name: External Attacker — Cloud Misconfiguration Hunter
threat_actors.motivation: Gain access to publicly exposed cloud storage buckets or APIs to steal raw or curated data at scale
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Publicly accessible data lake bucket, exposed Spark UI, or unauthenticated Kafka broker endpoint
non_capabilities: No valid credentials for any tier at the start
No zero-day budget — relies on misconfigurations and default settings
No physical access to any infrastructure
No access to internal network segments without lateral movement from an initial foothold

attack_paths.entry_point: Unauthenticated Kafka broker port (9092) or REST proxy exposed to external source network
attack_paths.impact: Unauthorized message production to any topic — enables data injection or queue flooding
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Kafka clusters in multi-cloud setups commonly lack mutual TLS; broker ports often network-accessible from peered VPCs containing untrusted sources

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious Spark job submitted via Airflow DAG modification or direct Spark REST API
attack_paths.impact: Arbitrary code execution on Spark cluster with access to all data lake zones and data warehouse
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Spark REST API on default port 6066 is unauthenticated by default; Airflow DAG repository often writable by data engineers

attack_paths.entry_point: Stolen data engineer credentials used to modify DAG definitions and trigger rogue pipeline jobs
attack_paths.impact: Pipeline manipulation — attacker controls data flow scheduling, can exfiltrate via new DAG tasks or suppress quality checks
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Airflow credentials are high-value; web UI often protected only by username/password without MFA

attack_paths.entry_point: Publicly accessible or over-permissioned S3/GCS bucket containing raw ingest data
attack_paths.impact: Bulk exfiltration of raw records before data quality filtering — may contain PII or sensitive operational data
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Public bucket misconfigurations are among the most common cloud data breaches; raw zones often have broader ACLs than curated zones

attack_paths.entry_point: Over-privileged BI dashboard service account or direct JDBC connection with exported credentials
attack_paths.impact: Bulk export of aggregated business-sensitive records from data warehouse
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: BI tools frequently cache service account credentials; warehouses often allow full SELECT without row-level filtering

attack_paths.entry_point: Spark job (AP-002) or Airflow DAG manipulation (AP-003) with write permissions to curated zone
attack_paths.impact: Deletion or overwrite of curated datasets — cascading failure across data warehouse, feature store, and ML models
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires earlier foothold; curated zone typically has tighter write permissions than raw zone

attack_paths.entry_point: Poisoned Flink streaming output injected via compromised external source (AP-001) sustained over multiple runs
attack_paths.impact: Corrupted feature vectors degrade ML model accuracy silently — high business impact over time without triggering alerts
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires sustained poisoning over multiple pipeline cycles; effect is gradual and hard to detect without feature distribution monitoring

attack_paths.entry_point: IAM role chaining via over-permissioned service accounts attached to Spark or Flink cluster nodes
attack_paths.impact: Escalation to storage admin privileges — full read/write access to all data lake zones and data warehouse
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Cloud IAM role misconfiguration is common in data platforms; node service accounts often carry excessive storage permissions for convenience

mitigations.control_name: Kafka mutual TLS and ACL-based topic access control
Spark job signing and submission allowlist — restrict to signed DAG-triggered jobs only
MFA enforcement on all Airflow web UI accounts; DAG repo protected by branch policies
Data lake bucket private-by-default policy; block public access at cloud org level
DLP monitoring on data warehouse export operations; row-level security enabled
Immutable versioning and object-lock on curated data lake zone
Feature distribution monitoring with statistical drift alerts
Least-privilege IAM roles for cluster node service accounts; no storage admin attachment

findings.severity_rationale: Unauthenticated Kafka broker access from external source networks allows arbitrary message injection into all topics, enabling poisoning of the entire pipeline from ingestion forward
Spark REST API without authentication allows arbitrary job submission with cluster-level data lake access — full data exfiltration or destruction in a single API call
Public-accessible raw data lake bucket exposes unfiltered PII-containing records before quality checks have processed them
Over-permissioned cluster IAM roles allow privilege escalation to storage admin without requiring additional credential compromise
Airflow DAG manipulation via stolen engineer credentials can redirect or suppress pipeline stages; MFA absence increases credential theft risk
Bulk data warehouse export without DLP or row-level controls allows insider exfiltration of aggregated business data at scale
Feature store poisoning requires sustained multi-run injection; object-lock on curated zone limits destruction path; detectable with distribution monitoring
Curated data lake destruction path mitigated by implemented object-lock versioning; residual risk limited to recovery time objective impact
